title: Derivators
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Grothendieck's proposal in Pursuing Stacks (1983, section 69) to keep all derived categories of diagram categories at once, with restriction functors that have adjoints on both sides. A nonzero morphism of arrows of complexes whose two components vanish, so that cones in a derived category cannot be chosen functorially; localization and prederivators; Kan's formulas and the derivator axioms; homotopy exact squares, pasting, finality of right adjoints, extension along sieves and cosieves; the derivator of a ring, through semifree and K-injective resolutions and discrete fibrations, and its strongness; pointed and stable derivators, and the stability of the derivator of a ring; a recognition lemma for cocartesian squares with Franke's detection criterion, composition and cancellation, and shifted derivators; additivity of stable derivators, with the flip of a suspension equal to minus the identity; the canonical triangulated structure; exactness of restriction and homotopy Kan extensions, the Dold-Puppe sequences, and the comparison with the classical triangles of the derived category of a ring, including the sign of the identification of the suspension with the shift.
prerequisites: categories, functors, natural transformations, limits, colimits and adjoint functors
complexes, cones and derived categories (programme lesson Complexes, cones and localization, Lemmas 1.1-1.2, Lemma 2.1, Theorems 4.2 and 5.1, Proposition 5.2)
semifree and K-projective resolutions over a ring (programme lesson Flat modules and K-flat resolutions, Theorem 3.4)
K-injective resolutions in Grothendieck abelian categories (programme lesson of that name, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, equation (5.1), Proposition 5.2)

checks.reading: Grothendieck, Pursuing Stacks, sections 68-70 (CC0 edition, arXiv:2111.01000v2, TeX ps4.tex lines 176-886), section 69 read in full on 19 Oct 2026. M. Groth, Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators (arXiv:1112.3840v2, author TeX), sections 1-3 and 4.1 read on 19 Oct 2026 for the definitions, the base change calculus, the combinatorial-model-category example and the pointed and stable notions. The proofs in the lessons were written for this course: the derivator of a ring is proved with semifree and K-injective resolutions and Kan extensions along discrete (op)fibrations instead of model structures; stability of the derivator of a ring is proved through the total complex of a square and the surjectivity of the cospan map for injective representations. Sections 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2 of Groth's paper read on 19 Oct 2026 for lessons 6-9; the proofs there were written for this course: a single recognition lemma derives the detection criterion, composition and cancellation, and the objectwise criterion; biproducts come from a coproduct of two degenerate squares; the inverse of the identity comes from collapse maps of a three-legged span; the comparison with the classical triangles of D(R) and its sign are computed at chain level.

open_obligations: Integration of homotopy types (Pursuing Stacks section 69, second half: the left Kan extension for the derivator of small categories by the total category of a cofibred category, Thomason's theorem) is a later lesson.

The derivator of a Grothendieck abelian category without enough projectives (sheaves of modules, quasi-coherent sheaves) is not constructed: lesson 4 builds left Kan extensions from semifree resolutions, which such categories lack. The stability argument of lesson 5 and lessons 6-9 apply once the derivator exists.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
